## Load libraries

```{r, echo=TRUE, message=FALSE}

library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)
library(dplyr)
library(ggpubr)
library(lme4)  # for mixed-effects models

```

## Load data

```{r}

# Load metadata
meta_sponges <- read_csv("meta_sponges.csv")
meta_sponges <- meta_sponges %>% 
  filter(!if_all(everything(), is.na))

# Load oocyte / female gamete data
oocytes_sponges <- read_csv("oocytes_sponges.csv")
oocytes_sponges <- oocytes_sponges %>% 
  filter(!if_all(everything(), is.na))

# Load spermatocysts data
sperm_sponges <- read_csv("spermatocysts_sponges.csv")
sperm_sponges <- sperm_sponges %>% 
  filter(!if_all(everything(), is.na))

```

## Clean up data

```{r}
# Clean column names (remove spaces/special characters)
names(meta_sponges) <- gsub(" ", "_", tolower(names(meta_sponges)))
names(oocytes_sponges) <- gsub(" |#", "", tolower(names(oocytes_sponges)))
names(sperm_sponges) <- gsub(" |#", "", tolower(names(sperm_sponges)))


# Convert dates and handle seasons
meta_sponges <- meta_sponges %>%
  mutate(
    coll_date = mdy(coll_date),
    coll_month = factor(coll_month, levels = month.name),
    coll_season = factor(coll_season, levels = c("Winter", "Spring", "Summer", "Fall"))
  )

# Create reproductive status flags
meta_sponges <- meta_sponges %>%
  mutate(
    reproductive = ifelse(reproductive_status == "reproductive", 1, 0),
    has_oocytes = ifelse(oocytes_present == "yes", 1, 0)
  )

# Clean oocyte measurements
oocytes_sponges <- oocytes_sponges %>%
  mutate(area = as.numeric(area))
```

# SUMMARY STATS

```{r}

library(dplyr)

#BY SPECIES BY STAGE
summary_by_species_stage <- oocytes_sponges %>%
  # Ensure stage_clean and species are cleaned
  mutate(
    species = trimws(as.character(species)),
    stage_clean = trimws(stage_clean)
  ) %>%
  group_by(species, stage_clean) %>%
  summarise(
    n_specimens = n_distinct(specimen_id),
    n_measurements = n(),
    mean_feret = mean(feret, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_feret = sd(feret, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_feret = median(feret, na.rm = TRUE),
    min_feret = min(feret, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_feret = max(feret, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  # Optional: order stages logically
  mutate(stage_clean = factor(stage_clean, 
                              levels = c("previtellogenic", "vitellogenic_I", 
                                         "vitellogenic_II", "late oocyte or embryo", "embryo", "prelarva", "larva")))

# View the table
print(summary_by_species_stage)

# BY SPECIES
summary_by_species <- oocytes_sponges %>%
  mutate(species = trimws(as.character(species))) %>%
  group_by(species) %>%
  summarise(
    n_specimens = n_distinct(specimen_id),
    n_measurements = n(),
    mean_feret = mean(feret, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_feret = sd(feret, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_feret = median(feret, na.rm = TRUE),
    min_feret = min(feret, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_feret = max(feret, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

print(summary_by_species)
```

## Summary Stats II

> How many specimen are reproductive; do all stages co-occur? 

```{r}

# Is there a sampling bias in date? 

meta_sponges %>%
  dplyr::count(species, coll_month) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = coll_month, y = n, fill = species)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  labs(title = "Sample Distribution Across Seasons")


#Which specimens are reproductive? 
# Summary table
meta_sponges %>%
  group_by(species) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(
    n_specimens = n(),
    n_reproductive = sum(reproductive == 1, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_non_reproductive = sum(reproductive == 0, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_unknown = sum(is.na(reproductive)),
    prop_reproductive = n_reproductive / (n_reproductive + n_non_reproductive)
  )


# Do stages co-occur?

comb_summary <- meta_sponges %>%
  mutate(across(c(oocytes_present, sperm_present, embryos_present),
                ~ . == "yes")) %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(stage_combo = paste(
    c(ifelse(oocytes_present, "oocytes", NA),
      ifelse(sperm_present, "Sperm", NA),
      ifelse(embryos_present, "Embryos", NA)),
    collapse = " + ")) %>%
  mutate(stage_combo = gsub("NA \\+ ", "", stage_combo),
         stage_combo = gsub("\\+ NA", "", stage_combo),
         stage_combo = gsub("NA", "None", stage_combo)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  group_by(species, stage_combo) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), .groups = "drop")

library(ggplot2)

ggplot(comb_summary, aes(x = stage_combo, y = species, fill = n)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white") +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "plasma") +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Co-occurrence of gamete stages per species",
       x = "Stage combination",
       y = "Species",
       fill = "Count") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```

## Oocyte comparisons

```{r}

library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(FSA)          # dunnTest
library(rcompanion)   # cldList
library(lme4)         # mixed model
library(emmeans)      # post‑hoc for mixed model
library(multcomp)     # for cld with emmeans
library(car)          # Levene's test

# Set seed for reproducible jitter
set.seed(123)

# Prepare oocyte data
oocyte_data <- oocytes_sponges %>%
  filter(stage_clean == "vitellogenic_I") %>%
  mutate(species = trimws(species))

# Compute specimen means
oocyte_means <- oocyte_data %>%
  group_by(species, specimen_id) %>%
  summarise(mean_feret = mean(feret, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")


oocyte_summary <- oocyte_data %>%
  group_by(species) %>%
  summarise(
    n_specimens = n_distinct(specimen_id),
    n_oocytes = n(),
    mean = mean(feret, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd = sd(feret, na.rm = TRUE),
    median = median(feret, na.rm = TRUE),
    min = min(feret, na.rm = TRUE),
    max = max(feret, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
print(oocyte_summary)

# 2. Overall Kruskal‑Wallis test
kw_oocyte <- kruskal.test(mean_feret ~ species, data = oocyte_means)
print(kw_oocyte)   # e.g., chi-squared = 10.5, df = 3, p = 0.015

# Dunn test on specimen means
dunn_test <- dunnTest(mean_feret ~ species, data = oocyte_means, method = "bh")
print(dunn_test)

# Generate compact letters
cld_letters <- cldList(P.adj ~ Comparison, data = dunn_test$res, threshold = 0.05)
print(cld_letters)

# ---- FIX: Map Group names to actual species names ----
# Create a lookup table: actual species name -> name without spaces
species_lookup <- data.frame(
  species = unique(oocyte_means$species),
  species_no_space = gsub(" ", "", unique(oocyte_means$species))
)

# Merge with cld_letters
letters_oocyte <- cld_letters %>%
  left_join(species_lookup, by = c("Group" = "species_no_space")) %>%
  # Now we have the correct 'species' column; add max_y for positioning
  left_join(
    oocyte_means %>%
      group_by(species) %>%
      summarise(max_y = max(mean_feret)),
    by = "species"
  ) %>%
  mutate(y_pos = max_y * 1.1)

# Check that mapping worked
print(letters_oocyte)

# Order species by mean size (as before)
species_order <- oocyte_means %>%
  group_by(species) %>%
  summarise(mean_size = mean(mean_feret)) %>%
  arrange(mean_size) %>%
  pull(species)

oocyte_means$species <- factor(oocyte_means$species, levels = species_order)
oocyte_data$species <- factor(oocyte_data$species, levels = species_order)
letters_oocyte$species <- factor(letters_oocyte$species, levels = species_order)

# Plot
set.seed(123)
ggplot() +
  geom_jitter(data = oocyte_data,
              aes(x = species, y = feret),
              width = 0.1, size = 1.5, alpha = 0.3, colour = "grey50") +
  geom_boxplot(data = oocyte_means,
               aes(x = species, y = mean_feret),
               width = 0.4, outlier.shape = NA, fill = "skyblue", alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_point(data = oocyte_means,
             aes(x = species, y = mean_feret),
             size = 3, colour = "blue") +
  geom_text(data = letters_oocyte,
            aes(x = species, y = y_pos, label = Letter),
            size = 5) +
  labs(x = "Species",
       y = "Vitellogenic oocyte diameter (µm)",
       title = "Vitellogenic oocyte size per species") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(legend.position = "none")



```

## Oocyte sensitivity test

```{r}

oocyte_cv <- oocyte_means %>%
  group_by(species) %>%
  summarise(CV = sd(mean_feret)/mean(mean_feret) * 100)
oocyte_cv 


library(dplyr)
library(FSA)

# Assume oocyte_means is already created (species, specimen_id, mean_feret)
# Ensure species is character (not factor) to avoid factor level issues
oocyte_means <- oocyte_means %>%
  mutate(species = as.character(species))

# Get unique specimen IDs
specimen_ids <- unique(oocyte_means$specimen_id)

# Create an empty list to store results for each iteration
sensitivity_results <- list()

# Loop over each specimen to leave out
for (i in seq_along(specimen_ids)) {
  
  # Subset data excluding the i-th specimen
  data_loo <- oocyte_means %>% filter(specimen_id != specimen_ids[i])
  
  # Check if at least two species remain (Dunn test requires at least two groups)
  if (n_distinct(data_loo$species) < 2) {
    message("Skipping specimen ", specimen_ids[i], ": fewer than 2 species left.")
    next
  }
  
  # Run Dunn test (Benjamini–Hochberg adjustment)
  dunn_loo <- tryCatch(
    dunnTest(mean_feret ~ species, data = data_loo, method = "bh"),
    error = function(e) NULL
  )
  
  if (!is.null(dunn_loo)) {
    # Extract the results table and add a column identifying the removed specimen
    res <- dunn_loo$res %>%
      mutate(removed_specimen = specimen_ids[i])
    sensitivity_results[[i]] <- res
  }
}

# Combine all results into one data frame
sensitivity_df <- bind_rows(sensitivity_results)

# View the full sensitivity table
print(sensitivity_df)

# Optional: count how many times each comparison was significant (P.adj < 0.05)
sensitivity_summary <- sensitivity_df %>%
  group_by(Comparison) %>%
  summarise(
    n_tests = n(),
    n_significant = sum(P.adj < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE),
    proportion_significant = n_significant / n_tests
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(proportion_significant))

print(sensitivity_summary)

# sensitivity analysis shows that the significant difference between Mycale loveni and Tedania kagalaskai is robust: it remained significant in 17 out of 19 iterations (89.5%). The other pairwise comparisons were never significant (or only once, likely due to chance).


```


## Larvae comparisons

```{r}


# Load required libraries (if not already loaded)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(FSA)
library(rcompanion)
library(stats)

# Filter larval stage and clean species names
larvae_data <- oocytes_sponges %>%
  filter(stage_clean == "larva") %>%
  mutate(species = trimws(species))

# Compute mean diameter per specimen (to avoid pseudoreplication)
larvae_means <- larvae_data %>%
  group_by(species, specimen_id) %>%
  summarise(mean_feret = mean(feret, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

# Summary table: number of specimens, mean, SD, min, max of specimen means
desc_stats <- larvae_means %>%
  group_by(species) %>%
  summarise(
    n_specimens = n(),
    mean = mean(mean_feret),
    sd = sd(mean_feret),
    min = min(mean_feret),
    max = max(mean_feret)
  )

print(desc_stats)

# Create a two‑level factor: "Mycale" vs "Others"
larvae_means <- larvae_means %>%
  mutate(group = factor(ifelse(species == "Mycale loveni", "Mycale", "Others")))

# Exact two‑sample permutation test
set.seed(123)   # for reproducibility
perm_mycale_vs_others <- oneway_test(mean_feret ~ group, data = larvae_means,
                                     distribution = "exact")
perm_mycale_vs_others


# Get unique species names
species_list <- unique(larvae_means$species)

# Matrix to store p‑values (lower triangle)
pairwise_p <- matrix(NA, nrow = length(species_list), ncol = length(species_list),
                     dimnames = list(species_list, species_list))

# Loop over all pairs
for (i in 1:(length(species_list)-1)) {
  for (j in (i+1):length(species_list)) {

    subdat <- larvae_means %>% 
      filter(species %in% c(species_list[i], species_list[j])) %>%
      mutate(species = factor(species))

    test <- coin::oneway_test(mean_feret ~ species,
                              data = subdat,
                              distribution = "exact")

    pairwise_p[j, i] <- as.numeric(coin::pvalue(test))
  }
}
# Print the lower triangle (comparisons)
print(pairwise_p)

## The following tests are not reported, as sample sizes are too small! - but just to explore a little more: 

kruskal.test(mean_feret ~ species, data = larvae_means)

library(FSA)
dunn_larvae <- dunnTest(mean_feret ~ species, data = larvae_means, method = "bh")
print(dunn_larvae$res)

# Order species by mean size (for consistent plotting)
species_order <- larvae_means %>%
  group_by(species) %>%
  summarise(mean_size = mean(mean_feret)) %>%
  arrange(mean_size) %>%
  pull(species)

larvae_means$species <- factor(larvae_means$species, levels = species_order)
larvae_data$species <- factor(larvae_data$species, levels = species_order)

# Create the plot
```

## Larvae sensitivity test 

```{r}

library(dplyr)
library(coin)

# Assume larvae_means is already created (species, specimen_id, mean_feret)
# Ensure species is character to avoid factor level issues
larvae_means <- larvae_means %>%
  mutate(species = as.character(species))

# Get unique specimen IDs
specimen_ids <- unique(larvae_means$specimen_id)

# Create lists to store results
results_mycale_vs_others <- list()   # for Mycale vs. Others
results_pairwise <- list()            # for all pairwise comparisons

## Not included in results - probably not meaningful if Tedania is completely taken out with only one specimen with larvae... 
# Loop over each specimen to leave out
for (i in seq_along(specimen_ids)) {
  
  # Subset data excluding the i-th specimen
  data_loo <- larvae_means %>% filter(specimen_id != specimen_ids[i])
  
  # Skip if fewer than 2 species remain (Mycale vs. Others needs both groups)
  if (n_distinct(data_loo$species) < 2) {
    message("Skipping specimen ", specimen_ids[i], ": fewer than 2 species left.")
    next
  }
  
  # ---- 1. Mycale vs. Others ----
  # Create group variable
  data_loo_group <- data_loo %>%
    mutate(group = factor(ifelse(species == "Mycale loveni", "Mycale", "Others")))
  
  # Only run if both levels present
  if (nlevels(data_loo_group$group) == 2) {
    test_mycale <- tryCatch(
      oneway_test(mean_feret ~ group, data = data_loo_group, distribution = "exact"),
      error = function(e) NULL
    )
    if (!is.null(test_mycale)) {
      res_mycale <- data.frame(
        removed_specimen = specimen_ids[i],
        comparison = "Mycale vs Others",
        p_value = as.numeric(pvalue(test_mycale)),
        stringsAsFactors = FALSE
      )
      results_mycale_vs_others[[i]] <- res_mycale
    }
  }
  
  # ---- 2. Pairwise comparisons ----
  # Get species present in this subset
  spp_present <- unique(data_loo$species)
  
  # Loop over all pairs (only if at least 2 species)
  if (length(spp_present) >= 2) {
    for (a in 1:(length(spp_present)-1)) {
      for (b in (a+1):length(spp_present)) {
        sp1 <- spp_present[a]
        sp2 <- spp_present[b]
        
        # Subset data for these two species
        pair_dat <- data_loo %>% filter(species %in% c(sp1, sp2))
        
        # Ensure both species have at least one observation
        if (n_distinct(pair_dat$species) == 2) {
          pair_dat <- pair_dat %>% mutate(species = factor(species))
          
          test_pair <- tryCatch(
            oneway_test(mean_feret ~ species, data = pair_dat, distribution = "exact"),
            error = function(e) NULL
          )
          if (!is.null(test_pair)) {
            res_pair <- data.frame(
              removed_specimen = specimen_ids[i],
              comparison = paste(sp1, "-", sp2),
              p_value = as.numeric(pvalue(test_pair)),
              stringsAsFactors = FALSE
            )
            # Store in list
            idx <- length(results_pairwise) + 1
            results_pairwise[[idx]] <- res_pair
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }
}

# Combine results into data frames
sensitivity_mycale <- bind_rows(results_mycale_vs_others)
sensitivity_pairwise <- bind_rows(results_pairwise)

# View summaries
print(sensitivity_mycale)
print(sensitivity_pairwise)

# Optional: summarise how often each comparison was significant (p < 0.05)
summary_pairwise <- sensitivity_pairwise %>%
  group_by(comparison) %>%
  summarise(
    n_tests = n(),
    n_significant = sum(p_value < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE),
    proportion_significant = n_significant / n_tests
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(proportion_significant))

print(summary_pairwise)

# For Mycale vs. Others:
summary_mycale <- sensitivity_mycale %>%
  summarise(
    n_tests = n(),
    n_significant = sum(p_value < 0.05),
    proportion_significant = n_significant / n_tests
  )
print(summary_mycale)

```


## Correlations

```{r}

# =============================================================================
# ENVIRONMENTAL INFLUENCES ON REPRODUCTIVE STATUS
# =============================================================================
#
# Aim:
# Test whether reproductive status is associated with:
#   - species
#   - depth
#   - latitude
#   - longitude
#   - collection month
#
# Final approach:
# Firth's penalized likelihood logistic regression is used because
# Tedania kagalaskai is completely separated (all specimens reproductive).
#
# The final model contains depth + species.
# =============================================================================


# =============================================================================
# 1. LOAD PACKAGES
# =============================================================================

library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)
library(logistf)
library(car)
library(ggplot2)


# =============================================================================
# 2. PREPARE DATA
# =============================================================================

meta_env_all <- meta_sponges %>%
    dplyr::select(
        specimen_id,
        species,
        reproductive_status,
        depth,
        lat,
        lon,
        coll_date
    ) %>%
    filter(
        !is.na(reproductive_status),
        !is.na(species),
        !is.na(depth),
        !is.na(lat),
        !is.na(lon),
        !is.na(coll_date)
    ) %>%
    mutate(
        # Binary response:
        # 1 = reproductive
        # 0 = non-reproductive
        reproductive_bin = if_else(
            reproductive_status == "reproductive",
            1,
            0
        ),

        # Species as categorical predictor
        species = factor(species),

        # Collection month
        month_num = month(coll_date)
    )


# =============================================================================
# 3. BASIC DATA CHECKS
# =============================================================================

str(meta_env_all)

# Number of specimens per species and reproductive status

table(
    meta_env_all$species,
    meta_env_all$reproductive_bin
)


# =============================================================================
# 4. DESCRIPTIVE SUMMARY OF REPRODUCTIVE STATUS
# =============================================================================

reproductive_summary <- meta_env_all %>%
    group_by(species, reproductive_bin) %>%
    summarise(
        n = n(),
        .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    group_by(species) %>%
    mutate(
        percentage = 100 * n / sum(n)
    ) %>%
    ungroup()

reproductive_summary


# =============================================================================
# 5. CHECK FOR COMPLETE SEPARATION
# =============================================================================

with(
    meta_env_all,
    table(species, reproductive_bin)
)

# Tedania kagalaskai has 0 non-reproductive and 7 reproductive specimens,
# resulting in complete separation in ordinary logistic regression.
#
# Therefore, Firth's penalized likelihood logistic regression is used
# for the final analysis.


# =============================================================================
# 6. FIRTH LOGISTIC REGRESSION: CANDIDATE MODELS
# =============================================================================
#
# Firth logistic regression is used throughout because of complete separation.
#
# Candidate models:
#   1. Species
#   2. Depth + species
#   3. Depth + latitude + species
#   4. Depth + longitude + species
#   5. Depth + species + longitude + month
#   6. Full model
#
# The main question is whether environmental predictors beyond depth
# improve the model sufficiently to justify their inclusion.
# =============================================================================


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 6a. Species-only model
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

m_species_firth <- logistf(
    reproductive_bin ~ species,
    data = meta_env_all
)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 6b. Depth + species
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

m_depth_species_firth <- logistf(
    reproductive_bin ~ depth + species,
    data = meta_env_all
)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 6c. Depth + latitude + species
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

m_depth_lat_species_firth <- logistf(
    reproductive_bin ~ depth + lat + species,
    data = meta_env_all
)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 6d. Depth + longitude + species
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

m_depth_lon_species_firth <- logistf(
    reproductive_bin ~ depth + lon + species,
    data = meta_env_all
)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 6e. Depth + longitude + month + species
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

m_depth_lon_month_species_firth <- logistf(
    reproductive_bin ~ depth + lon + month_num + species,
    data = meta_env_all
)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 6f. Full model
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

m_full_firth <- logistf(
    reproductive_bin ~ depth + lat + lon + month_num + species,
    data = meta_env_all
)


# =============================================================================
# 7. MODEL COMPARISON
# =============================================================================
#
# logistf does not provide the standard AIC.
#
# We therefore calculate an AIC-like criterion based on the penalized
# log-likelihood:
#
#   AIC-like = -2 × penalized log-likelihood + 2 × number of parameters
#
# Lower values indicate better relative model fit.
#
# This criterion is used only as a comparative measure among the
# Firth models.
# =============================================================================


firth_AIC_like <- function(model) {
    loglik_full <- as.numeric(model$loglik["full"])
    k <- length(model$coefficients)
    aic_like <- -2 * loglik_full + 2 * k
    return(aic_like)
}

firth_aic_table <- tibble(

    model = c(
        "Species",
        "Depth + species",
        "Depth + latitude + species",
        "Depth + longitude + species",
        "Depth + longitude + month + species",
        "Full model"
    ),

    AIC_like = c(
        firth_AIC_like(m_species_firth),
        firth_AIC_like(m_depth_species_firth),
        firth_AIC_like(m_depth_lat_species_firth),
        firth_AIC_like(m_depth_lon_species_firth),
        firth_AIC_like(m_depth_lon_month_species_firth),
        firth_AIC_like(m_full_firth)
    )
)

firth_aic_table %>%
    arrange(AIC_like)


# =============================================================================
# 8. LIKELIHOOD-RATIO TESTS
# =============================================================================
#
# Compare the simpler and more complex Firth models.
#
# NOTE:
# These comparisons should be interpreted cautiously because the sample
# size is small and Firth models use penalized likelihood.
#
# The primary criterion for the final model is parsimony together with
# consistency of the predictor effects.
# =============================================================================


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 8a. Does depth improve the species-only model?
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

anova(
    m_species_firth,
    m_depth_species_firth
)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 8b. Does latitude improve the depth + species model?
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

anova(
    m_depth_species_firth,
    m_depth_lat_species_firth
)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 8c. Does longitude improve the depth + species model?
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

anova(
    m_depth_species_firth,
    m_depth_lon_species_firth
)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 8d. Does month improve the depth + species model?
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

m_depth_month_species_firth <- logistf(
    reproductive_bin ~ depth + month_num + species,
    data = meta_env_all
)

anova(
    m_depth_species_firth,
    m_depth_month_species_firth
)


# =============================================================================
# 9. FINAL MODEL
# =============================================================================
#
# The final model contains depth + species.
#
# This model is preferred because:
#
#   - depth provides a clear improvement over the species-only model;
#   - species remains an important predictor;
#   - latitude, longitude and month do not provide sufficient evidence
#     to justify their inclusion;
#   - the model is more parsimonious and appropriate for the small sample.
# =============================================================================


final_model_firth <- logistf(
    reproductive_bin ~ depth + species,
    data = meta_env_all
)

summary(final_model_firth)


# =============================================================================
# 10. FINAL MODEL COEFFICIENTS
# =============================================================================

final_results <- tibble(
    term = names(final_model_firth$coefficients),
    beta = final_model_firth$coefficients,
    OR = exp(final_model_firth$coefficients),
    CI_lower = exp(final_model_firth$ci.lower),
    CI_upper = exp(final_model_firth$ci.upper),
    p_value = final_model_firth$prob
)

final_results


# =============================================================================
# 11. MULTICOLLINEARITY
# =============================================================================
#
# Assess multicollinearity among environmental predictors using the full
# model. This is retained as a diagnostic because latitude, longitude,
# depth and month were considered as candidate predictors.
# =============================================================================

vif_full <- vif(
    glm(
        reproductive_bin ~ depth + lat + lon + month_num + species,
        data = meta_env_all,
        family = binomial
    )
)

vif_full


# =============================================================================
# 12. PREDICTED PROBABILITIES ACROSS DEPTH
# =============================================================================
#
# Predictions are generated for each species across the observed depth range.
#
# Because the final model contains only depth and species, no other
# environmental variable needs to be held constant.
# =============================================================================

newdata_depth <- expand.grid(

    depth = seq(
        min(meta_env_all$depth),
        max(meta_env_all$depth),
        length.out = 100
    ),

    species = levels(meta_env_all$species)
)


newdata_depth$predicted_probability <- predict(
    final_model_firth,
    newdata = newdata_depth,
    type = "response"
)


# =============================================================================
# 13. PLOT PREDICTED PROBABILITIES
# =============================================================================

ggplot(
    meta_env_all,
    aes(
        x = depth,
        y = reproductive_bin,
        color = species
    )
) +

    geom_jitter(
        height = 0.05,
        width = 0,
        alpha = 0.6
    ) +

    geom_line(
        data = newdata_depth,
        aes(
            x = depth,
            y = predicted_probability,
            color = species
        ),
        linewidth = 1
    ) +

    labs(
        x = "Depth (m)",
        y = "Probability of reproductive status",
        color = "Species"
    ) +

    theme_minimal()


# =============================================================================
# 14. SPECIES-SPECIFIC ANALYSES
# =============================================================================
#
# These are exploratory/descriptive because sample sizes are small.
#
# Tedania kagalaskai is not analysed separately because all seven specimens
# are reproductive and therefore there is no variation in the response.
# =============================================================================


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Monanchora pulchra
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

mona_data <- meta_env_all %>%
    filter(species == "Monanchora pulchra")

m_mona_depth <- logistf(
    reproductive_bin ~ depth,
    data = mona_data
)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Mycale (Mycale) loveni
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

myca_data <- meta_env_all %>%
    filter(species == "Mycale (Mycale) loveni")

m_myca_depth <- logistf(
    reproductive_bin ~ depth,
    data = myca_data
)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Stelodoryx oxeata
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

stel_data <- meta_env_all %>%
    filter(species == "Stelodoryx oxeata")

m_stel_depth <- logistf(
    reproductive_bin ~ depth,
    data = stel_data
)


# =============================================================================
# 15. REPRODUCTIVE STAGES AND COLLECTION MONTH
# =============================================================================
#
# Separate descriptive analysis of reproductive stages.
#
# This is not used as a formal test of environmental effects because
# sampling across months is strongly unbalanced.
# =============================================================================

oocytes_df <- oocytes_sponges %>%

    left_join(
        meta_sponges %>%
            dplyr::select(
                specimen_id,
                coll_month
            ),
        by = "specimen_id"
    )


# Number of observations per collection month

table(oocytes_df$coll_month)


# Number of specimens per species and month

table(
    meta_sponges$species,
    meta_sponges$coll_month
)


# =============================================================================
# END OF ANALYSIS
# =============================================================================
```

```{r}

# Are oocyte size and larvae size correlated? 
# Create a species-level dataset
species_means <- bind_rows(

) %>% group_by(species) %>% summarise_all(mean, na.rm = TRUE)

# Correlation test
cor.test(species_means$oocyte_mean, species_means$larvae_mean, method = "spearman")


# =============================================================================
# Logistic regression analysis: environmental correlates of reproduction
# Data: meta_sponges with columns:
#   - reproductive_status : factor/character ("reproductive"/"non-reproductive")
#   - species             : factor
#   - depth               : numeric (m)
#   - lat                 : numeric (decimal degrees)
#   - lon                 : numeric (decimal degrees)
#   - coll_date           : Date (collection date)
#   - fixative            : factor (e.g., "EMA", "ethanol", "unknown")
#
# Species identity is included as a fixed effect in all comparative models.
# Collection month is evaluated as a continuous temporal predictor.
# Tedania kagalaskai is excluded from comparative modelling because all
# examined individuals were reproductive.
# =============================================================================

library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)
library(car)          # for vif()
library(broom)        # for tidy model output
library(ggplot2)
library(brglm2)       # for Firth's penalized likelihood (if needed)

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Prepare data
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Prepare data
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

meta_env <- meta_sponges %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(reproductive_status),
    !is.na(depth),
    !is.na(lat),
    !is.na(lon),
    !is.na(coll_date)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    reproductive_bin = ifelse(
      reproductive_status == "reproductive", 1, 0
    ),
    species = factor(species),

    # Collection month as a continuous variable (1–12). This is ok bc we don't have December or January e.g. 
    month_num = lubridate::month(coll_date)
  ) %>%
  drop_na(depth, lat, lon, month_num, species)

# Quick check of sample sizes
table(meta_env$species, meta_env$reproductive_bin)

## Here, we exclude Tedania now, because ALL individuals are reproductive, so the model doesnt work well. So we remove it
meta_env <- meta_clean %>%
  dplyr::filter(species != "Tedania kagalaskai") %>%
  droplevels()

table(meta_env$species, meta_env$reproductive_bin)

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Univariate models (each predictor + species)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Because species can explain a lot of variation, we include it in every model
# to test the additional effect of each environmental variable. Species is included in every model to test whether each environmental
# variable explains additional variation in reproductive status.

# Species-only model
m_species <- glm(
  reproductive_bin ~ species,
  data = meta_env,
  family = binomial
)
summary(m_species)

# Depth
m_depth <- glm(reproductive_bin ~ depth + species, 
               data = meta_env, family = binomial)
summary(m_depth)
# LRT: does depth improve the species-only model?
anova(m_species, m_depth, test = "Chisq")

# Latitude
m_lat <- glm(reproductive_bin ~ lat + species, 
             data = meta_env, family = binomial)
summary(m_lat)
anova(m_species, m_lat, test = "Chisq")

# Longitude
m_lon <- glm(reproductive_bin ~ lon + species, 
             data = meta_env, family = binomial)
summary(m_lon)
anova(m_species, m_lon, test = "Chisq")

# Collection month as a continuous predictor
m_month <- glm(
  reproductive_bin ~ month_num + species,
  data = meta_env,
  family = binomial
)
summary(m_month)
# LRT
anova(m_species, m_month, test = "Chisq")


# Fixative (but doesnt really makes sense for reproductive status - that should be for the sizes...) 
if("fixative" %in% names(meta_env)) {
  m_fix <- glm(reproductive_bin ~ fixative + species, 
               data = meta_env, family = binomial)
  summary(m_fix)
  anova(m_species, m_fix, test = "Chisq")
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Multivariable model building
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Start with a model containing all potentially relevant predictors.
# Choose the best representation of time: month_fct, month_num, or season.
# Based on univariate results and sample size, decide.
# Here we illustrate using depth, lat, season, and species.

full_model <- glm(reproductive_bin ~ depth + lat + lon + month_num + species, 
                  data = meta_env, family = binomial)
summary(full_model)

# Check for multicollinearity (VIF)
vif(full_model)  # VIF > 5–10 indicates problematic collinearity

# Check for separation (perfect prediction) – if coefficients are huge with huge SEs,
# or if warnings about fitted probabilities 0 or 1 appear.
# If separation is present, consider Firth's correction:
if(any(grepl("separation", warnings()))) {
  full_model_firth <- glm(reproductive_bin ~ depth + lat + lon + month_num + species, 
                          data = meta_env, family = binomial, 
                          method = "brglmFit")  # from brglm2
  summary(full_model_firth)
}

# Model selection/simplification using likelihood ratio tests (manual backward elimination)
# Compare full model to model without depth
m_no_depth <- update(full_model, . ~ . - depth)
anova(m_no_depth, full_model, test = "Chisq")

# Without lat
m_no_lat <- update(full_model, . ~ . - lat)
anova(m_no_lat, full_model, test = "Chisq")

# Without longitude
m_no_lon <- update(full_model, . ~ . - lon)

anova(m_no_lon, full_model, test = "Chisq")

# Without collection month
m_no_month <- update(full_model, . ~ . - month_num)

anova(m_no_month,full_model,test = "Chisq")

# AIC-based selection (alternative) - not included in my results as not needed... 
step_model <- step(full_model, direction = "backward", trace = 0)
summary(step_model)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Final model interpretation

# Based on the current results, the final parsimonious model is:
# reproductive status ~ depth + lon + species
# BUT I also test a primary model, without longitude

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

final_model <- glm(
  reproductive_bin ~ depth + lon + species,
  data = meta_env,
  family = binomial
)

summary(final_model)

# Odds ratios
exp(coef(final_model))
# 95% confidence intervals for odds ratios
exp(confint(final_model))

final_model_br <- glm(
     reproductive_bin ~ depth + lon + species,
     data = meta_env,
     family = binomial,
     method = "brglmFit"
)
 
summary(final_model_br)
exp(coef(final_model_br))
confint(final_model_br)
exp(confint(final_model_br))

#Model without lon 
final_model_2 <- glm(
  reproductive_bin ~ depth + species,
  data = meta_env,
  family = binomial
)

summary(final_model_2)

# Odds ratios
exp(coef(final_model_2))
# 95% confidence intervals for odds ratios
exp(confint(final_model_2))


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Visualisation of predicted probabilities
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Create prediction data for each species over the range of a continuous variable
# while holding other variables constant (e.g., at median or reference level).

newdata_depth <- expand.grid(
  depth = seq(
    min(meta_env$depth),
    max(meta_env$depth),
    length.out = 100
  ),
  lon = median(meta_env$lon),
  species = levels(meta_env$species)
)

newdata_depth$pred <- predict(
  final_model_br,
  newdata = newdata_depth,
  type = "response"
)

# Plot
ggplot(
  meta_env,
  aes(x = depth, y = reproductive_bin, color = species)
) +
  geom_jitter(
    height = 0.05,
    width = 0,
    alpha = 0.6
  ) +
  geom_line(
    data = newdata_depth,
    aes(y = pred, color = species),
    linewidth = 1
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Depth (m)",
    y = "Probability of reproduction"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()


# Separate panels by species
ggplot(
  meta_env,
  aes(x = depth, y = reproductive_bin)
) +
  geom_jitter(
    height = 0.05,
    width = 0,
    alpha = 0.6
  ) +
  geom_line(
    data = newdata_depth,
    aes(y = pred),
    linewidth = 1
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~ species) +
  labs(
    x = "Depth (m)",
    y = "Probability of reproduction"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 7. Species-specific descriptive models
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

  meta_env,

stel_data <- filter(

# Inspect species-specific models if needed
m_myca_lat

# =============================================================================
# REPRODUCTIVE STAGES AND COLLECTION MONTH
# =============================================================================
#
# This is a descriptive analysis of reproductive-stage composition across
# collection months. It is kept separate from the logistic regression of
# reproductive status.
# =============================================================================

oocytes_df <- oocytes_sponges %>%
  left_join(
    meta_sponges %>%
      dplyr::select(
        specimen_id,
        coll_month
      ),
    by = "specimen_id"
  )


# Check structure
glimpse(oocytes_df)


stage_order <- c(
  "previtellogenic",
  "vitellogenic_I",
  "vitellogenic_II",
  "late oocyte or embryo",
  "embryo",
  "prelarva",

)

# Convert to ordered factor
oocytes_df$stage_clean <- factor(
  oocytes_df$stage_clean,
  levels = stage_order,

)


# Determine the most advanced reproductive stage per specimen
specimen_stage <- oocytes_df %>%
  group_by(

  ) %>%

    has_embryo = any(
      stage_clean %in% c("embryo", "prelarva", "larva")
    ),
    has_larvae = any(
      stage_clean %in% c("prelarva", "larva")
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    max_stage = factor(
      max_stage,
      levels = stage_order,
      ordered = TRUE
    )
  )


# Count specimens per species and month
```

# SPERMATOCYSTS

> Measurements of sperm heads 

```{r}

# Sperm head diameters of individual spermatocysts in four sponge species. Each point represents a single sperm cell, colored by specimen of origin.
# Spermatocysts are globally ordered from left to right by decreasing mean sperm head diameter across all species. Black diamonds indicate the mean head diameter for each spermatocyst. 
# Facets separate species, allowing comparison of cyst-level and specimen-level variation within and among species.


library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(lme4)
library(lmerTest)      # for p‑values in summary
library(emmeans)       # for pairwise comparisons
library(performance)   # for ICC and diagnostics
library(car)           # for ANOVA (if needed)
library(patchwork)     # for combining plots (optional)
library(RColorBrewer)

sperm <- sperm_sponges %>%
  # Clean species names (if needed)
  mutate(species = trimws(species)) %>%
  # Create a unique cyst ID: species + specimen + spermatocyst number
  mutate(cyst_id = paste(species, specimen_id, spermatocyst_, sep = "_")) %>%
  # Ensure specimen_id and cyst_id are factors (for random effects)
  mutate(
    specimen_id = factor(specimen_id),
    cyst_id = factor(cyst_id)
  )

# Check sample sizes per level
sperm %>%
  group_by(species) %>%
  summarise(
    n_specimens = n_distinct(specimen_id),
    n_cysts = n_distinct(cyst_id),
    n_sperm = n()
  )

desc_species <- sperm %>%
  group_by(species) %>%
  summarise(
    n_specimens = n_distinct(specimen_id),
    n_cysts = n_distinct(cyst_id),
    n_sperm = n(),
    mean_head = mean(head_diameter, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_head = sd(head_diameter, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_head = median(head_diameter, na.rm = TRUE),
    min_head = min(head_diameter, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_head = max(head_diameter, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
print(desc_species)

desc_specimen <- sperm %>%
  group_by(species, specimen_id) %>%
  summarise(
    n_cysts = n_distinct(cyst_id),
    n_sperm = n(),
    mean_head = mean(head_diameter, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_head = sd(head_diameter, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
print(desc_specimen)



if (!"cyst_id" %in% colnames(sperm)) {
  sperm <- sperm %>%
    mutate(cyst_id = paste(species, specimen_id, spermatocyst_, sep = "_"))
}

# --- 2. Compute cyst means (one row per cyst) ---
cyst_means <- sperm %>%
  group_by(species, specimen_id, cyst_id) %>%
  summarise(mean_head = mean(head_diameter, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

# --- 3. Order cysts within each species by mean_head (increasing) ---
cyst_order <- cyst_means %>%
  group_by(species) %>%
  arrange(desc(mean_head), .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(cyst_ord = row_number()) %>%   # 1 = smallest mean head diameter
  ungroup()

# --- 4. Attach cyst order and cyst mean to the raw data ---
sperm_cyst <- sperm %>%
  left_join(cyst_order %>% dplyr::select(cyst_id, cyst_ord, mean_head), by = "cyst_id")

# --- 6. Set species order (by overall mean, optional) ---
species_order <- sperm %>%
  group_by(species) %>%
  summarise(mean_head = mean(head_diameter)) %>%
  arrange(mean_head) %>%
  pull(species)
sperm_cyst$species <- factor(sperm_cyst$species, levels = species_order)

# --- 7. Create colour palette for specimens ---
specimen_ids <- unique(sperm_cyst$specimen_id)
n_specimens <- length(specimen_ids)
if (n_specimens <= 9) {
  specimen_palette <- brewer.pal(n_specimens, "Set1")
} else {
  specimen_palette <- colorRampPalette(brewer.pal(8, "Set2"))(n_specimens)
}
names(specimen_palette) <- specimen_ids

# --- 8. Build the publication figure ---
p2_publication <- ggplot(sperm_cyst, aes(x = cyst_ord, y = head_diameter)) +
  # Raw data points
  geom_point(aes(colour = specimen_id), 
             position = position_jitter(width = 0.1), 
             alpha = 0.5, size = 1.2) +
  # Cyst means (black diamonds)
  geom_point(aes(y = mean_head), colour = "black", shape = 18, size = 3) +
  # Facet by species, free x-scale
  facet_wrap(~ species, scales = "free_x", nrow = 1) +
  # Colour scale
  scale_colour_manual(values = specimen_palette, name = "Specimen") +
  # Labels
  labs(x = "Spermatocysts (ordered by increasing mean head diameter)",
       y = "Sperm head diameter (µm)") +
  # Theme
  theme_bw(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.title = element_text(size = 12),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 10),
    strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey90"),
    strip.text = element_text(size = 14, face = "italic"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.spacing = unit(1, "lines")
  ) +
  # Sample size annotations
  geom_text(data = sperm_cyst %>% 
              group_by(species) %>% 
              summarise(
                n_spec = n_distinct(specimen_id),
                n_cyst = n_distinct(cyst_id),
                x = Inf, y = Inf,
                .groups = "drop"
              ),
            aes(x = x, y = y, 
                label = paste0("n_spec = ", n_spec, "\nn_cyst = ", n_cyst)),
            inherit.aes = FALSE, hjust = 1.1, vjust = 1.5, size = 3.5, colour = "black")

# --- 9. Display the plot ---
print(p2_publication)



p1_publication <- ggplot(sperm, aes(x = species, y = head_diameter)) +
  geom_violin(fill = "grey90", alpha = 0.7, trim = FALSE) +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.2, outlier.shape = NA, alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.15, alpha = 0.3, size = 1, colour = "grey30") +
  labs(x = "Species", y = "Sperm head diameter (µm)") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, face = "italic"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  ) +
  # Optional: add sample sizes below x‑axis
  geom_text(data = sperm %>% group_by(species) %>% summarise(n = n()),
            aes(x = species, y = -Inf, label = paste0("n = ", n)),
            vjust = -0.5, size = 3.5, inherit.aes = FALSE)

print(p1_publication)

## STATS

m_base <- lmer(head_diameter ~ species + (1 | specimen_id) + (1 | cyst_id),
               data = sperm)

# Residual plot
plot(m_base)

# QQ plot of residuals
qqnorm(resid(m_base))
qqline(resid(m_base))

# Shapiro–Wilk test (large sample – may be significant even if close)
shapiro.test(resid(m_base))

# Homogeneity of variance (plot residuals vs fitted)

m_log <- lmer(log(head_diameter) ~ species + (1 | specimen_id) + (1 | cyst_id),
              data = sperm)

# Check residuals again
plot(m_log)
qqnorm(resid(m_log))
qqline(resid(m_log))

# Assuming meta_sponges has columns: specimen_id, coll_month, depth
sperm2 <- sperm %>%
  left_join(meta_sponges %>% dplyr::select(specimen_id, coll_month, depth), by = "specimen_id") %>%
  # Convert month to numeric (1–12) and create sine/cosine for cyclic pattern
  mutate(
    month_num = as.numeric(as.character(coll_month)),  # adjust if coll_month is factor
    sin_month = sin(2 * pi * month_num / 12),
    cos_month = cos(2 * pi * month_num / 12),
    depth_sc = scale(depth)  # standardise depth
  )

m_month_factor <- lmer(log(head_diameter) ~ species + coll_month +
                         (1 | specimen_id) + (1 | cyst_id),
                       data = sperm2)

m_depth_lin <- lmer(log(head_diameter) ~ species + depth_sc +
                      (1 | specimen_id) + (1 | cyst_id),
                    data = sperm2)
m_depth_quad <- lmer(log(head_diameter) ~ species + depth_sc + I(depth_sc^2) +
                       (1 | specimen_id) + (1 | cyst_id),
                     data = sperm2)

anova(m_depth_lin, m_depth_quad)  # test quadratic term


# Use the best‑fitting model (e.g., m_species or m_month)
emm_species <- emmeans(m_species, ~ species)
pairs(emm_species, adjust = "tukey")

# Compact letter display
library(multcomp)
cld(emm_species, adjust = "tukey", Letters = letters)


# From the log-transformed model (m_log or m_depth_quad)
icc(m_depth_quad)
VarCorr(m_depth_quad)

# Boxplot of cyst means per species
cyst_means %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = species, y = mean_head)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.2, alpha = 0.5) +
  labs(y = "Mean sperm head diameter per cyst (µm)") +
  theme_bw()
```

```{r} 

library(sf)
library(rnaturalearth)
library(rnaturalearthdata)
library(ggplot2)

# Map for our collections

world <- ne_countries(scale = "medium", returnclass = "sf")

ggplot(data = world) +
  geom_sf(fill = "gray95", color = "gray80") +
  geom_point(data = meta_sponges, aes(x = lon, y = lat, color = depth, shape = species), #can also do species as color if needed 
             size = 2, alpha = 0.7) +
  coord_sf(xlim = c(-181, -132), ylim = c(50, 61), expand = FALSE) +
  labs(title = "Sampling locations in Alaska by species",
       x = "Longitude", y = "Latitude", color = "Depth [m]") +
  theme_bw()


ggplot(data = world) +
  geom_sf(fill = "gray95", color = "gray80") +
  geom_point(data = meta_sponges, 
             aes(x = lon, y = lat, color = species),  # color by species
             size = 2, alpha = 0.7) +
  coord_sf(xlim = c(-181, -132), ylim = c(50, 61), expand = FALSE) +
  labs(title = "Sampling locations in Alaska by species",
       x = "Longitude", y = "Latitude", 
       color = "Species") +  # updated legend title
  theme_bw()


# Prepare specimen data
meta_sponges <- meta_sponges %>%
  filter(!is.na(lon), !is.na(lat)) %>%           # remove any missing coordinates
  mutate(lon_360 = ifelse(lon < 0, lon + 360, lon))  # convert to 0–360 for mapping

# (Optional) set species order for legend
meta_sponges <- meta_sponges %>%
  mutate(species = factor(species, levels = c("Monanchora pulchra", 
                                              "Mycale (Mycale) loveni", 
                                              "Stelodoryx oxeata", 
                                              "Tedania kagalaskai")))

# Base map (already shifted)
world_shifted <- st_shift_longitude(ne_countries(scale = "medium", returnclass = "sf"))

# Choose map limits – either use the same as before or adjust to points
xlim_final <- c(160, 260)   # covers Aleutians to Gulf of Alaska
ylim_final <- c(50, 62)      # adjust if points extend further south/north

# Create the map
map_specimens <- ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = world_shifted, fill = "gray95", color = "gray70", size = 0.2) +
  geom_point(data = meta_sponges,
             aes(x = lon_360, y = lat, color = species),
             size = 2, alpha = 0.8) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Monanchora pulchra" = "blue",
                                 "Mycale (Mycale) loveni" = "red",
                                 "Stelodoryx oxeata" = "yellow",
                                 "Tedania kagalaskai" = "green")) +  # match the earlier colors
  coord_sf(xlim = xlim_final, ylim = ylim_final, expand = FALSE) +
  labs(title = "Sampling locations in Alaska by species",
       x = "Longitude", y = "Latitude", color = "Species") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 10) +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank(),
        legend.position = "bottom") +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = c(160, 180, 200, 220, 240),
    labels = function(x) {
      dplyr::case_when(
        x == 160 ~ "160°E",
        x == 180 ~ "180°",
        x == 200 ~ "160°W",
        x == 220 ~ "140°W",
        x == 240 ~ "120°W",
        TRUE ~ as.character(x)
      )
    }
  )

print(map_specimens)




# Map with distribution ranges from OBIS
library(ggplot2)
library(sf)
library(rnaturalearth)
library(viridis)
library(dplyr)

# Prepare data (assuming obis_360 and world_shifted already created)
# Ensure species_clean is a factor with levels in desired order
obis_360 <- obis_360 %>%
  filter(species_clean != "Other") %>%
  mutate(species_clean = factor(species_clean))

# Compute bounding box of all records (with 2° buffer)
x_range <- range(obis_360$lon_360)
y_range <- range(obis_360$decimalLatitude)

xlim_data <- c(x_range[1] - 2, x_range[2] + 2)
ylim_data <- c(y_range[1] - 2, y_range[2] + 2)

mycale_range <- obis_360 %>%
  filter(species_clean == "Mycale loveni") %>%
  summarise(min_lat = min(decimalLatitude), max_lat = max(decimalLatitude))
print(mycale_range)

# Let's check Mycale's latitude range:
obis_360 %>%
  filter(species_clean == "Mycale loveni") %>%
  summarise(min_lat = min(decimalLatitude), max_lat = max(decimalLatitude))

# If it's, say, 48–62, then set ylim = c(48, 65) to include all.

# Choose final limits (example using data range with a buffer)
xlim_final <- c(160, 260)   # still covers the Pacific-centered longitudes of interest
ylim_final <- c(30, 71)      # adjust based on Mycale's minimum

# Ensure obis_360 has species_clean and lon_360
# (Assuming already prepared as per previous steps)

# Shifted world map
world_shifted <- st_shift_longitude(ne_countries(scale = "medium", returnclass = "sf"))

# Create the map
map_hex <- ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = world_shifted, fill = "gray99", color = "gray70", size = 0.2) +
  geom_hex(data = obis_360,
           aes(x = lon_360, y = decimalLatitude, fill = after_stat(count)),
           bins = 30, alpha = 0.8) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(
    name = "Number of\nrecords (log)",
    option = "plasma",
    trans = "log10",                # log transform to handle wide count range
    labels = scales::label_number()  # show actual numbers (not log)
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~ species_clean, nrow = 2) +
  coord_sf(xlim = xlim_final, ylim = ylim_final, expand = FALSE) +
  labs(title = "OBIS record density per species",
       x = "Longitude", y = "Latitude") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 10) +
  theme(
    strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey90"),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "italic", size = 10),
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "bottom"
  ) +
scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = c(160, 180, 200, 220, 240),
    labels = function(x) {
      dplyr::case_when(
        x == 160 ~ "160°E",
        x == 180 ~ "180°",
        x == 200 ~ "160°W",
        x == 220 ~ "140°W",
        x == 240 ~ "120°W",
        TRUE ~ as.character(x)
      )
    }
  )
print(map_hex)
```

## THORSEN'S RULE

```{r}

## Test of Thorsons Rule :) 
# Have deeper and polar species larger larvae? 

data <- read.csv("poecilosclerid_larvae.csv")

str(data)
names(data)
summary(data)

data <- data[, colSums(!is.na(data)) > 0]
data$Depth <- as.numeric(data$Depth)

# Latitude
data$latitude <- as.numeric(data$Approx..Latitude)
# Absolute latitude
data$abs_latitude <- abs(data$latitude)
# Larval size
data$larval_size <- as.numeric(data$Larvae.size)

# remove missing values for the model
d <- subset(data,
                  !is.na(larval_size) &
                    !is.na(abs_latitude) &
                    !is.na(Depth))

ggplot(d, aes(abs_latitude, larval_size)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  theme_classic() +
  labs(
    x = "Absolute latitude",
    y = "Larval size (µm)"
  )

#Test if larvae get bigger with latitude
m <- lm(log10(larval_size) ~ abs_latitude, data = d)
summary(m)

# Is there a family signal? 
lm(log10(larval_size) ~ abs_latitude + Family, data = d)

ggplot(d, aes(x = abs_latitude, y = Depth, color = Family)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  theme_classic() +
  labs(
    x = "Absolute latitude",
    y = "Depth",
    color = "Family"
  )

d$log_larval <- log10(d$larval_size)

## Remove cladorizidae because they might bias the analysis... 
d_no_carn <- subset(d, Family != "Cladorhizidae")


m_full <- lm(log_larval ~ abs_latitude + Depth, data = d)
m_no_carn <- lm(log_larval ~ abs_latitude + Depth, data = d_no_carn)

summary(m_full)
summary(m_no_carn)


library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)


p1 <- ggplot(d_no_carn,
             aes(x = abs_latitude,
                 y = log_larval,
                 color = Family)) +
  geom_point(size = 3, alpha = 0.85) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm",
              se = FALSE,
              color = "black") +
  theme_classic() +
  labs(
    x = "Absolute latitude (°)",
    y = expression(Log[10]~"larval size (µm)"),
    title = "A"
  ) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold")
  )

p2 <- ggplot(d_no_carn,
             aes(x = Depth,
                 y = log_larval,
                 color = Family)) +
  geom_point(size = 3, alpha = 0.85) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm",
              se = FALSE,
              color = "black") +
  theme_classic() +
  labs(
    x = "Depth (m)",
    y = expression(Log[10]~"larval size (µm)"),
    title = "B"
  ) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold")
  )

p3 <- ggplot(d_no_carn,
             aes(x = abs_latitude,
                 y = Depth,
                 color = Family)) +
  geom_point(size = 3, alpha = 0.85) +
  theme_classic() +
  labs(
    x = "Absolute latitude (°)",
    y = "Depth (m)",
    title = "C"
  ) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "right",
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold")
  )

final_fig <- (p1 | p2) / p3 +
  plot_layout(guides = "collect") &
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

final_fig

## STATS for dataset without carnivorous sponges - only filter feeding sponges!

summary(m_lat)$coefficients

anova(m_depth, m_both) # does latitude improve model beyond depth?
```
